question: The bump phase was plotted against the scene orientation θ for each epoch, from the same fish as in panel a, to compare the bump–scene mapping across the pre-learning, learning and post-training epochs, with black dashed reference lines indicating bump phase = θ in the pre- and post-training epochs and bump phase = 2θ (mod 2π) in the learning epoch.

analyse_plan.Objective: Compare the mapping between scene orientation and bump phase across the pre-learning, learning and post-learning epochs.
analyse_plan.Validation Checks: Verify that bump phase is calculated from the selected HD cells with the reported population-level readout. Confirm that scene orientation and bump phase are expressed in the same angular coordinates across epochs. Check that the epoch labels are assigned correctly.
analyse_plan.Steps: 1. Load Data: Load the scene-orientation time series θ, the decoded bump-phase time series, and the epoch labels for the same fish used in panel a of the symmetry experiment. 2. Validate Angle Format: Confirm that both θ and bump phase are represented in radians and will be interpreted modulo 2π before plotting. 3. Segment by Epoch: Split the full recording into the pre-learning, learning and post-training epochs according to the experiment labels. 4. Prepare Epoch-wise Plot Data: For each epoch, pair every scene-orientation sample with the corresponding bump-phase sample and assemble the scatter-plot coordinates. 5. Define Reference Mappings: For the pre- and post-training epochs, define the dashed-line reference as bump phase = θ; for the learning epoch, define the dashed-line reference as bump phase = 2θ (mod 2π). 6. Apply Common Axes: Set the same axis limits, angular units and plotting conventions across the three epochs so that the relationships can be compared directly. 7. Save Key Results: Save the epoch-wise scatter coordinates and the corresponding reference-line definitions for downstream checking, reuse and figure regeneration. 8. Visualization: Render the bump-phase-versus-θ scatter plots for the three epochs and overlay the black dashed reference lines for the appropriate mapping in each epoch. 9. Quality Control: Verify that the pre- and post-training plots are aligned with the diagonal mapping and that the learning-epoch plot is aligned with the slope-2 mapping rather than the diagonal.

key_analysis_results: The bump phase was plotted against the scene orientation θ for each epoch, from the same fish as in panel a, and in the symmetric scene the bump phase hugged the line with slope 2 instead of the diagonal. In the pre- and post-training epochs, the black dashed lines indicate bump phase = θ, whereas in the learning epoch they indicate bump phase = 2θ (mod 2π).
key_analysis_conclusions: In the symmetric scene, 180° of the visual scene is mapped on to the full 360° array of the HD neurons.

summary_report.abstract: The bump phase was plotted against the scene orientation θ for each epoch, from the same fish as in panel a, showing that in the pre- and post-training epochs the black dashed lines indicate bump phase = θ, whereas in the learning epoch they indicate bump phase = 2θ (mod 2π). In the symmetric scene, that is, during the learning epoch, the bump phase hugged the line with slope 2 instead of the diagonal.
summary_report.methods: For the same fish as in panel a, the bump phase and the scene orientation θ were taken across the pre-learning, learning and post-training epochs of the symmetric-scene experiment. The bump phase was plotted against θ separately for each epoch as an epoch-wise scatter plot. Black dashed reference lines were overlaid to indicate bump phase = θ in the pre- and post-training epochs and bump phase = 2θ (mod 2π) in the learning epoch, with angular values treated modulo 2π and displayed with matched axis ranges across epochs.
summary_report.results: The epoch-wise scatter plots showed that the bump phase was plotted against the scene orientation θ for each epoch, from the same fish as in panel a. In the pre- and post-training epochs, the black dashed lines indicate bump phase = θ, whereas in the learning epoch they indicate bump phase = 2θ (mod 2π). Consistent with the main text, in the symmetric scene the bump phase hugged the line with slope 2 instead of the diagonal.
summary_report.discussion: This panel shows the population-level consequence of the ordered tuning rotation in an intuitive way: in the symmetric scene, the bump phase hugged the line with slope 2 rather than the diagonal. This means that, in the symmetric scene, 180° of the visual scene is mapped on to the full 360° array of the HD neurons, whereas the pre- and post-training epochs follow the ordinary bump phase = θ relation.
